messages:
alex: Hey folks — after yesterday's kernel-routing tweak I see a regression in streamed-response latency for low-token budgets. p95 for short streams jumped from ~110ms -> ~220ms. Not sure if it's batch formation or KV warmup. Anyone else seeing this?

eng-bot: Deploy 2026-03-05T14:12 applied to cluster-us-west-2 (route: kernel-v2-default).

dmitri: Yep saw it in canary. Traced to lots of tiny batches (1-3 requests) that now prefer small-kernel path which disables the fast KV prefetch. KV hit rate fell in canary: 92% -> 58%.

sophie: Interesting — are partial-decodes being scheduled differently? We added preemptive partial-decode gating last week. Could interact with the coalesce window.

alex: I captured a short trace. Paste: ```
trace_id=0x7f3a
requests: 124 total
batch_size_distribution: {1: 48, 2: 36, 3: 20, >=4:20}
kernel_switches: small_kernel=82, large_kernel=42
kv_prefetches: 98
kv_reads: 210
kv_hit_rate: 0.58
partial_decode_preemptions: 15
avg_p95_latency_ms: 220
```

maria: From that: high count of 1-sized batches + partial preemptions = a lot of extra decode handoffs. When partial decode preempts it cancels the coalesced tail and forces an early flush; that removes the KV warmup benefit.

dmitri: Agreed. Hypothesis: kernel selection policy now biases small_kernel for short sequences which strips the KV-prefetch stage (fast path assumption). But for streamed responses that then extend, we lose warm KV entries. So token-budget-target tuning needs to be aware of streamed sessions.

sophie: We should try a two-priority admission: if client sets streaming=true OR predicted length > N, keep eligibility for the KV-prefetch path (even if seq len small). Test with predicted cutoff N=16 tokens. Also increase coalesce window by +6ms for streaming clients.

alex: Quick experiment results (canary -> 10k requests) after toggling: coalesce_window +6ms for streaming, keep-kv-prefetch for streaming clients: 
```
batch_size_distribution: {1: 30, 2: 40, 3: 25, >=4:5}
kv_hit_rate: 0.89
partial_decode_preemptions: 6
avg_p95_latency_ms: 125
cost_per_1k_tokens: -3% (due to fewer micro-batches)
```

maria: Nice. That suggests two levers: 1) prefer KV-prefetch for streaming-eligible requests, 2) slightly widen coalesce window for streaming. But need to guard cost/latency for non-streaming.

dmitri: Also saw kernel-hotpath imbalance: small_kernel has lower throughput for long streams due to repeated kernel swaps. Could add a fast-path that lets small_kernel call into the shared KV cache warmup code, or add a promoted-kernel decision after X tokens.

sophie: Implementation plan: 
- Metric: add streaming-tag to batch metrics and track kv_hit_rate_streaming vs non_streaming.
- Heuristic: streaming_keep_prefetch = true; streaming_coalesce_ms = base + 6ms.
- Kernel policy: if request_streaming && tokens_generated > 8 then promote to large_kernel to avoid repeated kernel-switch overhead.
- Safety: rollout as feature-flag with 10% -> 50% canary -> full.

alex: Also noticed a subtle perf regression in partial-decode scheduling loop where the preempt timer was compared in microseconds but coalesce window values had been accidentally stored as ms in one path. That mismatch caused early preempts. I raised PR #1248 to normalize units.

maria: Can you link the trace that shows the units mismatch? Tagging in the PR would help.

alex: Link: https://internal-traces/redwood/trace/0x7f3a and PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pull/1248. I added a unit test that exercises 1ms vs 1000us flows.

dmitri: Next steps: roll the streaming_keeps_prefetch flag to 10% on canary, gather kv_hit_rate_streaming, p50/p95, and partial_preempt_count. If metric regressions drop, expand. I'll take the rollout.

sophie: I'll add the instrumentation and a small synthetic workload that simulates 40% streaming short bursts + 60% non-streaming to validate costs.

maria: I'll watch ops metrics and set an alert if cost per token increases >8% or p95 for non-streaming increases >50ms.

alex: Cool — thanks. Tagging everyone for follow-up in this thread. :thumbsup:
